newsitem.title: CHINA: China to use CPI as benchmark for inflation.
newsitem.headline: China to use CPI as benchmark for inflation.

text.p: China plans to use consumer price inflation as its key indicator, gradually replacing its current use of retail price inflation as its benchmark, a senior economist said on Friday.

"The consumer price index can more accurately reflect price rises in consumer spending by urban and rural residents," Chen Dezun, director of the price research institute of the State Planning Commission, said in a telephone interview.
"We will gradually use consumer price inflation as the main indicator," he said.
However, he said the change reflected a shift in statistical methodology rather than a government policy adjustment.
The government had decided to gradually promote the consumer price index as the inflation benchmark, believing this would now more closely reflect national price increases, he said.
China's retail price index was based on sales prices of about 340 retail commodities including food, industrial consumer goods, oil products and coal, Chen said.

However, the consumer price index was based on purchase prices of retail commodities as well as prices of dozens of basic service items, thus covering a much broader range and more closely reflecting people's spending, he said.
China has up to now used retail price inflation as its benchmark to monitor inflation.
"That was because prices of almost all basic services were controlled by the state under a central planned economy," Chen said.

But price controls on services, including rents, water and gas and health care, had been partially relaxed as a result of economic reforms introduced since 1978 to push China's economy towards a market-driven system, he said.
"Spending on services is becoming larger and larger," he said.
But China was unlikely to use consumer price inflation as its sole indicator and would continue to monitor both retail and consumer price inflation, he said.
Beijing has this year for the first time set a target for consumer price inflation, Chen said. Its goal is eight percent, compared with 8.3 percent in 1996.
China's target for retail price inflation is six percent for 1997. Retail price inflation was 6.1 percent in 1996, down from 14.8 percent in 1995.
China's consumer price inflation was 5.2 percent in the first quarter, while retail price inflation was 2.6 percent.
